title: What If You Lost Your Sense of Smell? The Danger Isn't Food

scenes.text: What if you woke up unable to smell anything? The danger isn't the food.
About one in twenty people lose or have a disturbed sense of smell at some point, from viruses, sinus disease, or head injury.
Gas leaks, smoke, and spoiled milk would go unnoticed. Researchers describe serious near misses.
Eating changes too. Some people lose their appetite and weight; others drift toward fat, salt, and sugar.
Studies in the US and Scandinavia link smell loss to a higher risk of dying younger.
The surprise is emotional. Smell is tied to memory, so celebrations can feel flat, and many people report grief.
